decision.title: sxml:parse-code compiles each language's queries once; iXML compared with tree-sitter

body.p: , at the owner's request for a comparison of iXML with tree-sitter in the book's "Invisible XML Performance".

item.p: The bug the comparison found: sxml:parse-code compiled the highlights, locals and injections queries of an injected language for every injection. Markdown injects its inline grammar into every paragraph, so 1 MB of Markdown took 29 s, 97 % of it in ts_query_new. src/source_code.c now keeps a language_queries entry per language for the document: each layer's tree_analysis borrows the compiled queries (and the table of highlight captures) from it, and the document releases them at its end. The same input takes 1.1 s, 60 % of it tree-sitter's own parse; the trees are the same, element for element. No header changes.

The comparison: the benchmark suite parses 1 MB of JSON with an iXML grammar (tests/bench/ixml/json.ixml), with sxml:parse-code and with fn:json-to-xml, and the Markdown input with sxml:parse-code, with limits in --check like the other rows (COMPARISONS in tests/bench/run-ixml-bench.py). The chapter gives the limits, the element counts, and tree-sitter's parse alone (about 0.11 s for the JSON, measured once with a small C program against the vendored runtime, not part of the suite).
